chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Dawud al-Abzari, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'An angel calls out every day: O son of Adam! You are begetting for death, and amassing for perishing, and building for ruin.'

key_terms.لِدْ: Beget/produce (in the sense of generating or accumulating)

ai.seo_question: What does the angel call out to humanity every day regarding worldly life?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that an angel calls out to humanity daily, reminding them that their worldly accumulation and construction are ultimately for death, perishing, and ruin. This hadith serves as an exhortation to reflect on the transient nature of the world (dunya) and to prepare for the afterlife. In Shia tradition, this daily divine reminder underscores the concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere rejection of the world, but as a conscious detachment from its deceptive permanence, urging believers to build their legacy upon eternal spiritual foundations rather than fleeting material gains.
